ctx.en: He's only just paid off his credit card and he's splurging again. He never learns.

ctx.s: “再熬一次夜没关系吧？”“你上个月刚累病，又{好了伤疤忘了疼}了？”
ctx.en: "One more late night won't hurt, will it?" "You made yourself ill last month. Forgotten already?"

ctx.s: 人总是{好了伤疤忘了疼}，灾难一过，防范意识就淡了。
ctx.en: People always forget once the pain has passed: as soon as a disaster is over, their caution fades.

ctx.s: 去年被骗过一回，今年他又{好了伤疤忘了疼}，把钱借给了陌生人。
ctx.en: He was conned last year, and this year he forgot the lesson and lent money to a stranger again.

ctx.s: 这家工厂出过事故，可没过多久就{好了伤疤忘了疼}，安全检查又松了。
ctx.en: The factory had an accident, but before long it forgot the lesson and safety checks grew lax again.

bad.s: 手术以后，他的伤口很快就{好了伤疤忘了疼}。
bad.en: (meant: after the operation his wound healed quickly and stopped hurting)
bad.why: It is not about physical healing; it criticises forgetting a lesson and repeating a mistake.

bad.s: 她离婚以后很快走出了痛苦，{好了伤疤忘了疼}，现在很幸福。
bad.en: (meant: after her divorce she quickly got over the pain and is happy now)
bad.why: It blames someone for not learning from pain, so it cannot praise recovering and moving on.

cards.mean: a last desperate hope that one clutches at
cards.lit: a piece of straw that a drowning person grabs to save his life

use.how: Noun, often in 抓住救命稻草, 把…当成救命稻草, 最后一根救命稻草. Said of a slim hope clung to in a crisis, often one that will not really help.

near.diff: 及时雨 is help that arrives just in time and really works; 救命稻草 is a slim hope clutched at in desperation, often in vain.

cards.cue: The factory is days from bankruptcy and the owner pins everything on one small investor who has shown only vague interest. What is that investor to him?

ctx.s: 这份工作是他最后的{救命稻草}。
ctx.en: This job is his last hope.

ctx.s: 医生都说没办法了，她还是把那种偏方当成了{救命稻草}。
ctx.en: Even after the doctors said nothing could be done, she clung to that folk remedy as her last hope.

ctx.s: “你真觉得这个人能帮我们？”“他是我们唯一的{救命稻草}了。”
ctx.en: "Do you really think this man can help us?" "He's the only straw left to clutch at."

ctx.s: 公司快撑不下去了，老板像抓住{救命稻草}一样抓住了这笔订单。
ctx.en: With the company about to go under, the boss grabbed at this order like a drowning man at a straw.

ctx.s: 考前一晚，他把学长的笔记当成{救命稻草}，看了一整夜。
ctx.en: The night before the exam he clung to a senior student's notes like a lifeline and read them all night.

ctx.s: 有些骗子专门利用病人想抓住{救命稻草}的心理。
ctx.en: Some swindlers deliberately exploit patients' urge to clutch at any last hope.

bad.s: 我饿的时候，妈妈做的饭就是我的{救命稻草}。
bad.en: (meant: when I'm hungry, mum's cooking is my favourite comfort)
bad.why: It is a slim last hope in a real crisis, not an everyday comfort or treat.

bad.s: 消防员是我们城市的{救命稻草}。
bad.en: (meant: firefighters are our city's lifesavers)
bad.why: It does not mean a rescuer or lifesaver; it is a fragile last hope that one clutches at, often uselessly.

cards.mean: to have nothing to live on, to go hungry
cards.lit: to drink the cold north-west wind, because there is nothing else to eat

use.how: Verb phrase, mostly in complaints, warnings or rhetorical questions: 总不能喝西北风吧？ Said of having no income or nothing to eat, often as a threat of what will happen.

cards.cue: Your partner wants to quit his job tomorrow with no savings and no plan. You ask him how on earth you'll pay the rent and eat.

ctx.s: 你把工作辞了，我们全家{喝西北风}啊？
ctx.en: If you quit your job, what's the family supposed to live on, thin air?

ctx.s: 不挣钱怎么行，总不能{喝西北风}吧。
ctx.en: You've got to earn money; we can't live on fresh air.

ctx.s: 这个月工资又拖着不发，大家都快{喝西北风}了。
ctx.en: Our wages are late again this month; we'll all be starving soon.

ctx.s: 店里一个客人都没有，再这样下去，我们只能{喝西北风}了。
ctx.en: There isn't a single customer in the shop. If this goes on we'll have nothing to eat.

ctx.s: 他把钱全投进股市，结果赔光了，一家人差点{喝西北风}。
ctx.en: He put all his money into the stock market and lost the lot; his family nearly went hungry.

ctx.s: 老人常说，手艺学好了，走到哪儿都不会{喝西北风}。
ctx.en: The old folks always say that if you learn a trade properly, you'll never go hungry wherever you are.

bad.s: 冬天我喜欢站在外面{喝西北风}，很舒服。
bad.en: (meant: in winter I love standing outside in the cool breeze)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with enjoying the wind; it means having nothing to live on.

bad.s: 尊敬的各位来宾，由于经济危机，许多家庭不得不{喝西北风}。
bad.en: (meant, in a formal speech: because of the economic crisis many families fell into poverty)
bad.why: It is a jokey spoken complaint and sounds flippant in a formal speech about real hardship; say xianru kunjing or shenghuo kunnan.

cards.mean: to take advantage of a loophole or oversight
cards.lit: to squeeze through the gaps

use.how: Verb-object phrase that can split: 钻法律的空子, 钻了不少空子, 让人钻空子. Said of exploiting gaps in rules or supervision for one's own gain.

near.diff: 走后门 gets favours through personal connections; 钻空子 exploits a gap in the rules without anyone's help.

cards.cue: A shop's return policy forgets to say items must be unworn, so a customer buys a dress, wears it to a wedding and returns it for a refund. What is she doing?

ctx.s: 规定写得不清楚，难怪有人{钻空子}。
ctx.en: The rules are badly written; no wonder people exploit the loopholes.

ctx.s: 他利用公司报销制度的漏洞，{钻了不少空子}。
ctx.en: He took advantage of the gaps in the company's expenses system more than a few times.

ctx.s: “这样做不违法吧？”“不违法，但是在{钻法律的空子}。”
ctx.en: "This isn't illegal, is it?" "No, but it's exploiting a legal loophole."

ctx.s: 门卫一走开，几个学生就{钻了个空子}溜了出去。
ctx.en: The moment the guard stepped away, a few students seized the chance and slipped out.

ctx.s: 合同一定要写清楚，免得对方{钻空子}。
ctx.en: The contract must be written clearly so the other party can't exploit any loopholes.

ctx.s: 新政策一出台，就有商家想{钻空子}，用假材料骗补贴。
ctx.en: As soon as the new policy came out, some businesses tried to game it, using fake documents to claim subsidies.

bad.s: 他很聪明，总能{钻空子}帮大家解决难题。
bad.en: (meant: he is clever and always finds ingenious solutions for everyone)
bad.why: It criticises exploiting loopholes for one's own gain; it is not praise for clever problem-solving.

bad.s: 我在墙上{钻空子}，挂了一幅画。
bad.en: (meant: I drilled a hole in the wall and hung a picture)
bad.why: It is only figurative; drilling a hole is zuan ge kong or da ge dong.

cards.mean: to dodge a question or request with vague, evasive answers
cards.lit: to do tai chi, turning every push aside with soft, circling moves

use.how: Verb-object phrase, often 跟某人打太极 or 别打太极了; can split (打起太极). Said of someone who meets a question or request with vague talk instead of a clear yes or no.

near.diff: 踢皮球 is several people or departments pushing a job onto each other; 打太极 is one person deflecting a question or request with vague words.
绕弯子 is talking around a point you do mean to make; 打太极 is dodging so as to avoid giving any answer at all.

cards.cue: You ask the landlord three times when he will fix the heating, and each time he says it is complicated, we will see, and changes the subject.

ctx.s: 我问他什么时候还钱，他又开始{打太极}。
ctx.en: I asked him when he'd pay me back, and he started dodging the question again.

ctx.s: 你就直说行不行，别跟我{打太极}了。
ctx.en: Can you just tell me straight? Stop giving me the runaround.

ctx.s: 记者追问了三次，那位发言人一直在{打太极}，什么也没说。
ctx.en: The reporter pressed him three times, but the spokesman kept dodging and said nothing at all.

ctx.s: “加薪的事您考虑得怎么样了？”“这个嘛，再研究研究。”老板又在{打太极}。
ctx.en: "Have you thought about my pay rise?" "Well, we'll look into it." The boss was dodging again.

ctx.s: 我一提买房的事，他就{打起太极}来，说以后再说。
ctx.en: Whenever I bring up buying a flat, he starts hedging and says we'll talk about it later.

ctx.s: 面对居民的质疑，那位局长一直在{打太极}，始终不肯正面回答。
ctx.en: Faced with residents' doubts, the bureau chief kept evading and never gave a straight answer.

bad.s: 他{打太极}了我的问题，什么都没回答。
bad.en: (meant: he dodged my question and answered nothing)
bad.why: It takes no direct object; put the person after gen (ta gen wo da taiji) or say ta dui wo de wenti da taiji.

bad.s: 他想向她表白，可是太害羞，一直在{打太极}。
bad.en: (meant: he wanted to tell her he liked her but was too shy and kept beating around the bush)
bad.why: It is dodging someone else's question or demand; for not getting to your own point, say rao wanzi.

cards.mean: quickly and deftly, without any fuss
cards.lit: three: down five, take away two, a quick bead move on the abacus

story.text: The phrase is a line from the traditional rhymes for adding on the Chinese abacus. To add three when there are not enough lower beads on the rod, you push down the upper bead worth five and take away two lower beads. A practised hand does it in a split second, so the line came to mean doing any job quickly and neatly.
story.source: 珠算口诀（算盘加法口诀）

use.how: Adverbial, usually followed by 就: 他三下五除二就修好了。 Said of finishing a practical task, a meal or a problem quickly and with ease.

near.diff: 快刀斩乱麻 is cutting decisively through a tangled problem; 三下五除二 is simply doing a task fast and with practised ease.

cards.cue: Your bike chain has come off. Your neighbour flips the bike over, and in under a minute the chain is back on and the wheel is spinning.

ctx.s: 他{三下五除二}就把饭吃完了。
ctx.en: He polished off his meal in no time.

ctx.s: 别看这道题难，老师{三下五除二}就解出来了。
ctx.en: The problem looked hard, but the teacher solved it in a flash.

ctx.s: 师傅打开机器，{三下五除二}换好了零件，电脑又能用了。
ctx.en: The repairman opened up the machine, swapped the part in a few quick moves, and the computer worked again.

ctx.s: “这些箱子得搬到什么时候？”“叫上小王，{三下五除二}就搬完了。”
ctx.en: "How long will it take to move all these boxes?" "Get Xiao Wang to help and it'll be done in no time."

ctx.s: 妈妈揉好面团，{三下五除二}包了一大盘饺子。
ctx.en: Mum kneaded the dough and whipped up a big plate of dumplings in no time.

ctx.s: 这份表格看着复杂，熟练的会计{三下五除二}就能填好。
ctx.en: The form looks complicated, but an experienced accountant can fill it in in a few minutes.

bad.s: 他做事特别细心，{三下五除二}，一张表要检查一整天。
bad.en: (meant: he is very careful and spends a whole day checking one form)
bad.why: It means fast and effortless, the opposite of slow, painstaking checking; for that say yi si bu gou.

bad.s: 她说话{三下五除二}，我一句也没听清。
bad.en: (meant: she talks so fast I couldn't catch a word)
bad.why: It describes getting a task done quickly, not how fast someone talks; say ta shuohua tai kuai.

cards.mean: to act at once while conditions are favourable
cards.lit: to hammer the iron while it is still hot

use.how: Verb phrase, often first in a clause followed by the action: 趁热打铁，马上…… Said of following up at once on a success, a good mood or fresh interest.

near.diff: 一鼓作气 is finishing a task in one unbroken burst of energy; 趁热打铁 is seizing a favourable moment before it cools.

cards.cue: Your team has just won a big client and everyone is excited. Your boss says to pitch to their sister company this week, before the buzz fades.

ctx.s: 老师刚讲完，你就{趁热打铁}做几道练习吧。
ctx.en: The teacher has just explained it, so strike while the iron is hot and do a few exercises.

ctx.s: 第一本书卖得很好，出版社想{趁热打铁}，明年就出续集。
ctx.en: The first book sold well, so the publisher wants to strike while the iron is hot and bring out a sequel next year.

ctx.s: “他好像对这套房子挺满意的。”“那就{趁热打铁}，今天把合同签了。”
ctx.en: "He seems pretty happy with the flat." "Then strike while the iron's hot and get the contract signed today."

ctx.s: 她跟男朋友刚和好，我劝她{趁热打铁}，把婚期定下来。
ctx.en: She had just made up with her boyfriend, so I urged her to seize the moment and set a wedding date.

ctx.s: 球队连赢三场，教练决定{趁热打铁}，加练新战术。
ctx.en: After three straight wins, the coach decided to strike while the iron was hot and drill new tactics.

ctx.s: 展会大获成功后，市政府{趁热打铁}，又推出了一系列扶持政策。
ctx.en: After the trade fair's great success, the city government followed up at once with a series of support measures.

bad.s: 饭菜要凉了，大家{趁热打铁}快吃吧。
bad.en: (meant: the food is getting cold, so eat it while it's hot)
bad.why: It is about seizing a favourable moment, not about hot food; for that say chen re chi.

bad.s: 考试没考好，心情很差，我决定{趁热打铁}，先好好睡一觉。
bad.en: (meant: I did badly in the exam, so I decided to rest first)
bad.why: It means pushing ahead at once while things are going well; resting after a setback is the opposite.

cards.mean: (of someone written off) to make a sudden comeback
cards.lit: a dried salted fish flips itself over

use.how: Intransitive predicate, often with 终于 or 来个: 他终于咸鱼翻身了。 Said, often jokingly, of a person, team or firm that rises from the bottom after being written off.

near.diff: 东山再起 is someone who once had power or fame regaining it, and sounds more formal; 咸鱼翻身 is someone at rock bottom rising unexpectedly, and is casual.

cards.cue: A team that finished bottom of the league five years running suddenly wins the championship, and its fans can hardly believe it.

ctx.s: 他找了三年工作，今年终于{咸鱼翻身}了。
ctx.en: After three years of job hunting, he has finally turned things around this year.

ctx.s: 别灰心，谁说你没有{咸鱼翻身}的一天？
ctx.en: Don't lose heart. Who says your day to turn things around won't come?

ctx.s: 这家小公司快倒闭了，没想到靠一款游戏{咸鱼翻身}。
ctx.en: This small firm was about to go under, but against all odds one game turned its fortunes around.

ctx.s: “上次我考了倒数第一，这次全班第三！”“你这是{咸鱼翻身}啊！”
ctx.en: "Last time I came bottom, and this time I came third in the class!" "That's quite a comeback!"

ctx.s: 那支球队被球迷骂了好几年，今年总算{咸鱼翻身}，打进了决赛。
ctx.en: Fans slammed that team for years, but this year it finally bounced back and reached the final.

ctx.s: 我现在是个穷学生，等我{咸鱼翻身}了，请你吃大餐。
ctx.en: I'm a broke student now, but once I turn my fortunes around I'll treat you to a big dinner.

bad.s: 他从小成绩就是第一，这次又拿了第一，真是{咸鱼翻身}。
bad.en: (meant: he came top again, as he always has)
bad.why: It is for someone who was down or written off; a person who was always on top has nothing to rise from.

bad.s: 热烈欢迎老校长{咸鱼翻身}，重新回到学校工作！
bad.en: (meant, in a formal welcome speech: we warmly welcome our former head back to work at the school)
bad.why: It is casual and pictures the person as a worthless salted fish, which is rude in a formal welcome; say chongfan gangwei.

cards.mean: down to earth and in touch with ordinary people's lives
cards.lit: to take in the breath of the earth, to stay connected to the ground

use.how: Usually an adjective after 很、不、更: 这部电视剧很接地气。 Praises a person, work, policy or product for being close to everyday life and ordinary people.

near.diff: 平易近人 describes a person's manner as easy to approach; 接地气 is about content, style or decisions that reflect ordinary people's real lives.

cards.cue: A new TV drama shows families squeezing onto buses and arguing over the electricity bill, and viewers say it feels just like their own lives.

ctx.s: 这部电视剧拍得很{接地气}，大家都爱看。
ctx.en: This series feels so true to everyday life that everyone loves it.

ctx.s: 他虽然是大明星，说话却很{接地气}。
ctx.en: He's a big star, but he talks just like ordinary people.

ctx.s: “这个广告怎么样？”“太高冷了，不够{接地气}。”
ctx.en: "What do you think of this ad?" "Too aloof. It doesn't connect with ordinary people."

ctx.s: 新市长常去菜市场跟居民聊天，大家都说他很{接地气}。
ctx.en: The new mayor often chats with residents at the market, and everyone says he's very down to earth.

ctx.s: 这本书用身边的小事讲经济学，读起来特别{接地气}。
ctx.en: The book explains economics through everyday things, so it reads as very down to earth.

ctx.s: 政策要想落实，首先得{接地气}，多听听老百姓的意见。
ctx.en: If a policy is to work, it first has to be grounded in real life and listen to ordinary people.

bad.s: 这家餐厅装修豪华，一道菜上千块，非常{接地气}。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant is luxurious and very expensive)
bad.why: It praises what is close to ordinary people's lives; a luxury restaurant far beyond everyday budgets is the opposite.

bad.s: 领导要多{接地气}群众，了解他们的困难。
bad.en: (meant: leaders should get closer to the public and learn about their difficulties)
bad.why: It takes no object; say lingdao yao duo jie diqi, or duo jiechu qunzhong (have more contact with the public).

cards.mean: one's trump card, the decisive move kept for the end
cards.lit: the killing blow with a jian, an old iron-bar weapon, kept for the decisive moment

use.how: Noun, often after 拿出、使出、亮出, or as 是……的杀手锏. Said of the decisive weapon, product, skill or argument held back to win. Also written 撒手锏.

near.diff: 王牌 is one's best card or best person in general; 杀手锏 stresses the decisive move brought out to settle a contest.

cards.cue: The talks are stuck. Then your boss calmly produces a rival's lower quote, which he had been holding back all along, and the other side gives in.

ctx.s: 低价是这家网店的{杀手锏}。
ctx.en: Low prices are this online shop's secret weapon.

ctx.s: 眼看就要输了，他终于使出了{杀手锏}。
ctx.en: Just as he was about to lose, he finally played his trump card.

ctx.s: “你怎么说服你爸的？”“我拿出了{杀手锏}：让奶奶帮我说话。”
ctx.en: "How did you talk your dad round?" "I played my trump card: I got Grandma to put in a word for me."

ctx.s: 这款手机的{杀手锏}是拍照，夜景拍得特别清楚。
ctx.en: This phone's killer feature is its camera; night shots come out really sharp.

ctx.s: 比赛只剩最后一局，他才用上{杀手锏}：一种对手从没见过的发球。
ctx.en: With only the last game left, he finally brought out his secret weapon: a serve his opponent had never seen.

ctx.s: 谈判陷入僵局时，我方才亮出{杀手锏}，对方只好让步。
ctx.en: Only when the talks reached deadlock did our side play its trump card, and the other side had to give way.

bad.s: 警察终于抓住了那个{杀手锏}。
bad.en: (meant: the police finally caught the killer)
bad.why: It is a decisive move or weapon, never a person who kills; for a killer say shashou.

bad.s: 他{杀手锏}了对手，赢得了比赛。
bad.en: (meant: he beat his opponent with a decisive move and won)
bad.why: It is a noun and cannot be used as a verb; say ta shichu le shashoujian (he played his trump card).

cards.r: yǒu yǎn bù shí tài shān
cards.mean: to fail to recognise someone of great standing or talent
cards.lit: to have eyes and still not recognise Mount Tai, the greatest of mountains

use.how: Predicate, most often 我真是有眼不识泰山, a polite apology on learning who someone really is; also used of others who failed to see a person's standing.

near.diff: 看走眼 is any misjudgement of a person or thing; 有眼不识泰山 is failing to see that someone is important or highly skilled.

cards.cue: At the pool you give a stranger tips on his stroke, then learn he is a former national swimming champion. What do you say with an embarrassed laugh?

ctx.s: 原来您就是王教授！我真是{有眼不识泰山}。
ctx.en: So you're Professor Wang! Forgive me for not knowing who you were.

ctx.s: 我刚才{有眼不识泰山}，说话多有得罪，请您别见怪。
ctx.en: I didn't realise who you were just now; please forgive anything rude I said.

ctx.s: 保安不让他进门，后来才知道他是公司老板，后悔自己{有眼不识泰山}。
ctx.en: The guard wouldn't let him in, then found out he was the company's owner and regretted not recognising him.

ctx.s: “你知道他是谁吗？全国象棋冠军！”“哎呀，我{有眼不识泰山}，还想教他下棋呢。”
ctx.en: "Do you know who he is? The national chess champion!" "Oh no, I had no idea, and I was trying to teach him chess!"

ctx.s: 店员看老人穿得朴素就不理他，真是{有眼不识泰山}，人家可是著名画家。
ctx.en: The shop assistant ignored the old man because he was plainly dressed, without realising he was a famous painter.

ctx.s: 小说里，客栈掌柜{有眼不识泰山}，把来访的大侠当成了穷书生。
ctx.en: In the novel, the innkeeper fails to recognise the great swordsman and takes him for a poor scholar.

bad.s: 我近视很严重，晚上开车总是{有眼不识泰山}。
bad.en: (meant: I'm very short-sighted and can't see well when driving at night)
bad.why: It is about failing to recognise an important person, not about poor eyesight.

bad.s: 你眼光真好，一眼就看出他是专家，真是{有眼不识泰山}！
bad.en: (meant: praising someone for spotting an expert at once)
bad.why: It means failing to see someone's standing, so it cannot praise a person who saw it at once.

cards.r: bàn lù shā chū ge chéng yǎo jīn
cards.mean: an unexpected rival appears midway and upsets the plan
cards.lit: halfway along the road, out charges a Cheng Yaojin

story.text: Cheng Yaojin was a real general of the early Tang dynasty, but he is best known as a hero of the Sui and Tang storytelling tradition and the novel Shuo Tang, where he is rough, comic and famously lucky. In a well-known episode he lies in wait on the road and robs a convoy carrying tribute silver to the court. The saying pictures someone like him leaping out halfway along your road.

use.how: A whole clause, often after 结果、没想到、谁知: 本来都谈好了，结果半路杀出个程咬金。 Said half-jokingly of a rival or obstacle that turns up unexpectedly and spoils a plan.

cards.cue: You had all but agreed to buy a flat when, the night before signing, another buyer turned up from nowhere and offered more.

ctx.s: 本来冠军是他的，没想到{半路杀出个程咬金}。
ctx.en: The title should have been his, but out of nowhere someone came along and snatched it.

ctx.s: 我们差点就签约了，结果{半路杀出了个程咬金}，另一家公司报价更低。
ctx.en: We had almost signed when a rival popped up from nowhere: another firm quoted a lower price.

ctx.s: “你不是要跟她约会吗？”“别提了，{半路杀出个程咬金}，她前男友回来了。”
ctx.en: "Weren't you going on a date with her?" "Don't ask. Out of nowhere, her ex came back."

ctx.s: 班长选举本来只有两个人竞争，后来{半路上杀出个程咬金}，局面全变了。
ctx.en: Only two people were running for class monitor, then a surprise candidate jumped in and changed everything.

ctx.s: 这块地眼看就要拍下了，谁知{半路杀出个程咬金}，把价格抬高了一倍。
ctx.en: We were about to win the land at auction when someone suddenly jumped in and doubled the price.

ctx.s: 比赛最后十分钟，{半路杀出个程咬金}，一位无名小将连进两球。
ctx.en: In the last ten minutes an unknown youngster came from nowhere and scored twice.

bad.s: 他是一个{半路杀出个程咬金}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he is the kind of person who turns up unexpectedly)
bad.why: It is a whole clause describing an event, not a quality of someone's character, so it cannot modify a noun.

bad.s: 两支强队从一开始就是夺冠热门，决赛果然是他们相遇，真是{半路杀出个程咬金}。
bad.en: (meant: the two favourites met in the final, just as everyone expected)
bad.why: It is for an unexpected newcomer appearing midway; an outcome everyone predicted from the start is the opposite.

cards.r: guò wǔ guān zhǎn liù jiàng
cards.mean: to overcome one obstacle after another on the way to success
cards.lit: to get through five mountain passes and cut down six generals

story.text: In the novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Guan Yu, cut off from his sworn brother Liu Bei, stays for a time with Cao Cao. When he learns where Liu Bei is, he sets out to rejoin him, escorting Liu Bei's wives. The commanders guarding the passes on the way try to stop him, and Guan Yu fights his way through five passes, killing six generals. The episode comes from the novel, not from the historical records.

use.how: Predicate, often 一路过五关斩六将: 她一路过五关斩六将进入决赛。 Said of getting through a series of rounds, tests or rivals; also of telling one's past triumphs.

near.diff: 披荆斩棘 is pushing through hardship to open up a way; 过五关斩六将 is beating a series of rounds, tests or rivals one after another.

cards.cue: A candidate gets through the written test, a group interview and three rounds with managers before she finally receives the job offer.

ctx.s: 她一路{过五关斩六将}，进了决赛。
ctx.en: She fought her way through round after round and made it to the final.

ctx.s: 能进这家公司的人，都是{过五关斩六将}才拿到录用通知的。
ctx.en: Everyone who gets into this firm has had to clear hurdle after hurdle to win an offer.

ctx.s: “考研难吗？”“初试、复试、面试，简直是{过五关斩六将}。”
ctx.en: "Is it hard to get into a master's programme?" "First exam, second exam, interview: it's one hurdle after another."

ctx.s: 这部电影{过五关斩六将}，最终拿下了最佳影片奖。
ctx.en: The film beat rival after rival and finally won Best Picture.

ctx.s: 爷爷一喝酒就讲自己年轻时{过五关斩六将}的故事。
ctx.en: Whenever Grandpa has a drink, he tells stories of all the battles he won when he was young.

ctx.s: 这款新药{过五关斩六将}，通过了一轮又一轮试验，终于上市了。
ctx.en: The new drug cleared hurdle after hurdle, passing round after round of trials, and finally went on sale.

bad.s: 比赛第一轮他就被淘汰了，真是{过五关斩六将}。
bad.en: (meant: he was knocked out in the very first round)
bad.why: It means winning through one round after another; for an early defeat it says the opposite.

bad.s: 他{过五关斩六将}地吃完早饭，就去上班了。
bad.en: (meant: he quickly finished his breakfast and went to work)
bad.why: It is about winning through a series of trials or rivals, not about doing an everyday task quickly.

cards.mean: a one-off deal made with no thought for future dealings
cards.lit: a deal done with a single blow of the hammer

use.how: Noun, usually with 做 or 不是: 做一锤子买卖。 Mostly criticises a seller who cheats or cuts corners because they never expect to see you again; also any one-off arrangement.

near.diff: 杀鸡取卵 is destroying a lasting source of gain for a quick profit; 一锤子买卖 is a single deal with no thought of dealing again.

cards.cue: A stall at a tourist spot sells you a fake souvenir at triple the price, knowing you will never come back. What kind of business is that?

ctx.s: 景区里不少小店做的都是{一锤子买卖}。
ctx.en: A lot of little shops at tourist sites only care about fleecing you once.

ctx.s: 做生意要讲信用，不能做{一锤子买卖}。
ctx.en: In business you have to keep your word; you can't treat every customer as a one-off.

ctx.s: “这家装修公司怎么样？”“别找他们，干完活就不管了，纯属{一锤子买卖}。”
ctx.en: "What's that renovation firm like?" "Avoid them. Once the job's done they don't care. It's strictly one deal and goodbye."

ctx.s: 我们跟这位客户是长期合作，不是{一锤子买卖}，价格上可以让一点。
ctx.en: Our work with this client is long-term, not a one-off, so we can give a little on price.

ctx.s: 这次合作就是{一锤子买卖}，项目结束以后大家各走各的。
ctx.en: This partnership is a one-off: when the project ends, we go our separate ways.

ctx.s: 有的网店靠虚假宣传赚快钱，做的都是{一锤子买卖}，很快就没了回头客。
ctx.en: Some online shops make quick money with false advertising; they only deal with you once, and soon have no repeat customers.

bad.s: 他谈判特别快，{一锤子买卖}就把合同签了。
bad.en: (meant: he negotiates fast and signed the contract in one go)
bad.why: It is a one-off deal with no future in view, not a deal closed quickly; for speed say hen kuai jiu qian le.

bad.s: 这家老店做的是{一锤子买卖}，几十年来顾客都很信任它。
bad.en: (meant: this old shop has kept its customers' trust for decades)
bad.why: It describes dealing once with no regard for return customers, so it contradicts decades of trust.
